    02 / Résumé

    Research experience

    Undergraduate Researcher

    Missouri University of Science and Technology · October 2025–Present

    NPT Barostat limitations in Molecular-Dynamics Simulations

    • Tested the limits of the NPT barostat to get familiar with LAMMPS and the Mill, MS&T’s local high performance computer.
    • Used Linux, and C++
    • Built LAMMPS simulations of face-centered cubic argon to study atomic motion during heating and cooling, including models with 2,048 atoms.
    • Analyzed mean-squared displacement, pressure, and simulation cell dimensions to identify when diffusion slowed during cooling and distinguish solid-like behavior from changes in box shape.
    • Developed Slurm batch scripts and Gnuplot workflows to compare thermostat settings and integration timesteps across runs, track temperature fluctuations, and export atomic trajectories for visualization in OVITO.

    Undergraduate Researcher

    Missouri University of Science and Technology · Summer 2025

    Single-Crystal Growth and Physical Properties of Tb6Cr4Al43 | Presented July 27, 2025

    • Completed approximately 250 hours of experimental research and produced a usable Tb6Cr4Al43 single crystal for structural and magnetic characterization.
    • Investigated how the compound’s atomic arrangement and rare-earth/transition-metal interactions influence magnetic ordering, anisotropy, and transport behavior.
    • Used X-ray diffraction to study the unit cell and compare it with the Ho6Mo4Al43 structure.
    • Prepared resistivity samples and studied transport properties in a superconducting magnet system.
    • Temperature- and field-dependent resistivity measurements were interpreted as showing ferromagnetic behavior.
    • Observed a residual resistivity ratio near 1, indicating little change in resistivity between room and low temperature.
    • Measured increasing resistivity with magnetic field, consistent with normal-metal behavior; Hall-resistivity measurements were inconclusive because strong magnetic attraction interfered with the measurement.
    • Delivered a 30-minute technical presentation describing the project, methods, and findings to graduate students.

    Computational Materials Research

    Li3PS4 Vacancy Configurations · In Progress · Results presentation planned for May 2027 at Undergraduate research conference

    • Predicting the locations of the Lithium ions vacancies by creating a small neural network based on the configuration of PS4
    • Optimizing the PS4 to make the Li ions transfer easier. This will help to make charging batteries quicker, and their lifetime will last longer.
    • Developed Python models of β-Li₃PS₄ to investigate lithium-site occupancy and vacancy arrangements for solid-state battery electrolytes.
    • Reconstructed neutron-diffraction crystal structures and built interactive 3D visualizations using ASE and PyXtal.
    • Implemented Monte Carlo simulations with a MACE interatomic potential to study temperature-dependent lithium occupancies and relative free energies.
    • Built simulation validation, convergence diagnostics, uncertainty estimation, and checkpointing workflows.
